claims: Named native-only-mocked tests require terminal state plus an explicit valid final numeric exit code, rejecting missing/invalid fields, still-running results and contradictory failed-plus-zero instead of inferring zero or one.
Named tests prevent startup-code inheritance, preserve valid native nonzero/negative statuses and exercise late log delivery, bounded drain and timer cleanup.
Existing native-mocked nonterminal and contradictory-failure tests now require safe protocol rejection rather than synthetic guest status.
limitations: Only named local command-completion regressions are covered; live provider behavior, other operation contracts and full capability coverage remain unverified.
No clean dependency installation or native-provider execution was performed; the existing installed dependency store was reused.
Installed native SDK contracts were inspected at the recorded version; compatibility throughout the declared dependency range is unverified.
Ordinary native errors retain the existing synthetic exit127 policy; protocol rejection does not itself guarantee remote cleanup or process-tree reaping.
Terminal status labels alone do not prove numeric success or failure; no output checksum or raw transport integrity is established.
The bounded log-drain timer is not an overall timeout guarantee: final stream wait, kill and logs operations still depend on native settlement.
command: pnpm --filter @computesdk/blaxel --fail-if-no-match exec vitest run src/__tests__/command-contract.test.ts src/__tests__/run-command.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --minWorkers=1
scope: Historical revision-specific local regression evidence, not all-capability or current/future-tree native certification.
